_comment: Documented divergences of the PHP event surface against the reference event_stream corpus (comparison block events_envelopes: expected keys only, volatile fields dropped recursively, absent fields recorded as null). Fail-closed: a failing case NOT listed here is red; a listed case that now passes is red (stale baseline); a case with no driver that is NOT listed is red. Root causes: (1) the reference's handler-level emitters (sus_patterns, ip_ban envelopes, security_headers, redis manager, ip extraction, decorators, dynamic-rule violation events) are not ported or are expressed as adapter seams without envelopes; (2) PHP block events ride the check pipeline bus (SecurityCheckPipeline::fireBlockHook) so their reasons are the on_block log-format strings and their metadata is the check-hook shape (check_name/trigger_info/status_code) instead of the reference's per-event metadata; (3) SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType maps only the eight pipeline check families, so blocks outside that map fall to the default penetration_attempt type. 4.3.2 corpus regen note: the reference generation environment does not have the optional guard_agent module installed, and the reference engine builds every middleware-bus SecurityEvent through guard_core._pydantic_plugin_mute.get_telemetry_model('SecurityEvent'), which imports guard_agent, so the construction fails closed and the reference capture harness recorded ZERO envelopes for every bus-emitted scenario; the corpus therefore pins expected: [] for them (verified live against the reference engine, which still captures 0 events for these cases). Two consequences, both applied in this ledger update: (a) the scenarios where the port emits nothing anyway now compare 0 against 0 and PASS, so five stale entries were removed (evt_behavioral_violation_usage_log, evt_ip_unbanned, evt_path_excluded_health, evt_pattern_detected_xss, evt_security_bypass_all) - their documented port gaps are unchanged but no longer produce a diff under this corpus revision; those passes ride on the corpus artifact, and a corpus regen with guard_agent installed will pin real envelopes again and resurface them as failures needing entries; (b) the scenarios where the port DOES emit (country_blocked, geo_lookup_failed) now diverge at count level against the zero pins and gained entries. If the corpus regenerates with guard_agent installed, every entry tied to a zero pin must be re-evaluated (stale entries are red by policy).

cases.evt_penetration_attempt_blocked: The PHP pipeline classifies the body XSS block under the suspicious_activity check, so SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType maps it to suspicious_request with the check-hook metadata shape (fireBlockHook); the reference emits penetration_attempt with request_count/trigger_info metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (suspicious_request, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_penetration_attempt_passive: PHP passive mode returns the request without a block response, so SecurityCheckPipeline::fireBlockHook never runs and the bus emits nothing for the block; the reference's passive dispatch emits a logged_only penetration_attempt. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 1 (security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_ip_blocked_global_blacklist: The PHP bus reason is the composed log format 'IP not allowed: <ip> - <detail>' and the metadata is the check-hook shape (SecurityCheckPipeline::fireBlockHook); the reference envelope carries the bare detail reason with filter_type metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (ip_blocked, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_ip_banned_then_blocked: The engine emits only the ip_blocked envelope: the ban-time event is an adapter-authored BanEventSink call (src/Ban/BanEventSink.php) carrying just (ip, duration, reason), so the corpus ip_banned envelope (handler ip_ban, metadata.duration) has no in-engine emitter. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (ip_blocked, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_ip_ban_failed_escalation: No PHP seam: the corpus ipban_fault injection has no analogue (IpBanManager has no raisable ban hook), and no PHP source emits ip_ban_failed anywhere; the runner's driver throws for the corpus call.
cases.evt_cloud_blocked_provider: The pipeline emits the cloud_blocked envelope but no decorator_violation: route-level decorator events (handler middleware, decorator_type block_clouds) are not ported; the port's cloud block surfaces only through the check pipeline. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 4 (cloud_blocked, decorator_violation, cloud_blocked, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_https_enforced_redirect: EventBus::sendHttpsViolationEvent builds the https_enforced envelope but no engine code calls it: the enforce_https redirect returns through the check pipeline, so the emit falls to the default block mapping (penetration_attempt) with check-hook metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (penetration_attempt, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_decorator_violation_auth_required: No PHP seam for the decorator send_authentication_failed_event emitter; the PHP authentication_failed envelope comes only from the pipeline block mapping, which cannot carry injected decorator kwargs; the runner's driver throws for the corpus decorator_event call.
cases.evt_access_denied_decorator: No PHP seam: the reference BaseSecurityDecorator send_access_denied_event emitter has no port; the bus carries only the require_https decorator pair; the runner's driver throws for the corpus decorator_event call.
cases.evt_authentication_failed_decorator: No PHP seam for the decorator send_authentication_failed_event emitter; the PHP authentication_failed envelope comes only from the pipeline block mapping, which cannot carry injected decorator kwargs; the runner's driver throws for the corpus decorator_event call.
cases.evt_content_filtered_max_size: The request_size_content check blocks the oversized request with the reference reason ('Request size 64 exceeds limit: 10'), but SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType has no content-filtering mapping (the block falls to the default penetration_attempt) and no emitter carries the content_filtered decorator metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (penetration_attempt, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_country_blocked_geo: Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes for this scenario because the reference generation environment lacks the optional guard_agent module (reference bus event construction fails closed, so the capture harness recorded zero); the port's geo_country_stub driver emits 1 country_blocked envelope through its own bus, so the runner sees got 1 want 0.
cases.evt_geo_lookup_failed_download: Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes for this scenario because the reference generation environment lacks the optional guard_agent module (reference bus event construction fails closed, so the capture harness recorded zero); the port's geo_download_failure driver emits 1 geo_lookup_failed envelope through its own bus, so the runner sees got 1 want 0.
cases.evt_csp_violation_report: No PHP seam: SecurityHeadersPolicy computes header maps only; the reference security_headers_manager's validate_csp_report / csp_violation agent event is not ported; the runner's driver throws for the corpus csp_report call.
cases.evt_custom_request_check_reject: The custom_request check blocks with the injected 418 response, but SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType maps custom_request to the default penetration_attempt and the bus reason is the generic 'Request blocked'; the reference emits custom_request_check with response_status/check_function metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (penetration_attempt, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_emergency_mode_block: The PHP emergency_mode check reason is the log-format '[EMERGENCY MODE] Access denied for IP <ip>' with check-hook metadata; the reference envelope reason is '[EMERGENCY MODE] IP <ip> not in whitelist' with emergency metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (emergency_mode_block, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_pattern_added_custom: No PHP seam: SusPatterns carries no custom-pattern registry surface, so no pattern_added envelope exists; the runner's driver throws for the corpus add_pattern call.
cases.evt_pattern_removed_custom: No PHP seam: SusPatterns carries no custom-pattern registry surface, so no pattern_removed envelope exists; the runner's driver throws for the corpus remove_pattern call.
cases.evt_rate_limited_global: The PHP rate-limit block reason is the composed log format 'Rate limit exceeded for IP: <ip> (N requests in Ws window)' and the emit rides the middleware handler with check-hook metadata; the reference envelope carries the bare 'Rate limit exceeded: ...' reason with a rate_limit handler and request_count metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (security_headers_applied, rate_limited).
cases.evt_dynamic_rule_violation_endpoint: The PHP endpoint-tier block emits rate_limited only; the reference's dynamic_rule_violation middleware emit for endpoint-specific limits has no PHP emitter. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (security_headers_applied, rate_limited).
cases.evt_rate_limit_script_reloaded: No envelope seam: the RateLimitHandler NOSCRIPT recovery reloads the script silently (src/RateLimit/RateLimitHandler.php) and its onScriptReloaded callback carries no envelope; the reference's rate_limit_script_reloaded agent event is not emitted; the runner's driver throws for the corpus rate_limit_script_reload call.
cases.evt_dynamic_rules_update_apply: DynamicRuleManager::sendRuleEvent emits through the middleware bus (handler middleware, reason 'Dynamic rules <id> v<n>', method SYSTEM), not the reference dynamic_rules handler envelope (reason 'Received/Applied updated rules ...', ip system, previous_version metadata). Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (dynamic_rule_updated, dynamic_rule_applied).
cases.evt_emergency_mode_activated: The PHP DynamicRuleManager emits dynamic_rule_updated/applied but has no emergency_mode_activated emitter; the emergency lockdown path logs only. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (dynamic_rule_updated, dynamic_rule_applied).
cases.evt_redis_connection_established: No PHP seam: the port's RedisHandler has no manager-level agent surface; the reference RedisManager emits redis_connection from initialize; the runner's driver throws for the corpus redis_connect call.
cases.evt_redis_error_connection_failed: No PHP seam: the port's RedisHandler has no manager-level agent surface; the reference RedisManager emits redis_error from a failed initialize; the runner's driver throws for the corpus redis_connect_error call.
cases.evt_route_unresolved_strict: No PHP emitter: routeResolutionStrict parses into SecurityConfig but no engine code consumes it, so the reference's route_unresolved emit has no analogue. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 1 (security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_security_headers_applied_default: No driver and no emitter: the port's SecurityHeadersPolicy computes headers on demand with no agent surface (KNOWN_GAPS, security headers management); the reference's headers_applied event is not emitted.
cases.evt_user_agent_blocked_global: The PHP user-agent block reason is the composed log format 'Blocked user agent: <ua>' with check-hook metadata; the reference envelope reason is "User agent '<ua>' in global blocklist" with filter_type metadata. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 2 (user_agent_blocked, security_headers_applied).
cases.evt_suspicious_request_untrusted_proxy: No PHP seam: extracting a client IP behind an untrusted proxy emits nothing in the port; the reference's ip_extraction spoofing seam in extract_client_ip has no analogue. Under the 4.3.2 corpus the divergence is count-level: the corpus pins 0 envelopes (reference bus event construction fails closed without the optional guard_agent module in the generation environment) while the port emits 1 (security_headers_applied).
